intro: Welcome to Van Museum, a museum in Van province, founded in 1972. It is one of the few museums anywhere with an Urartian collection of this depth: the bronze belts, helmets and cuneiform tablets from Çavuştepe, Ayanis and Toprakkale.
history: Founded in 1972, the museum gathers the finds from excavations at the Urartian centres around Lake Van: Çavuştepe, Ayanis and Toprakkale. Its bronze belts, helmets, horse harness and cuneiform tablets make one of the fullest collections of Urartian metalwork anywhere. The group of stelae found at Hakkâri is displayed here too.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Urartian bronzes and the cuneiform tablets. Linger over the finds from Ayanis, and end with the Hakkâri stelae.
facts: Did you know? The Hakkâri stelae turned up during building work, and because they resemble no known Anatolian tradition, which people made them is still argued over. And the museum's collection of Urartian bronzes is among the fullest anywhere, with belts, helmets and horse harness gathered in a single hall.
outro: This brings our tour of Van Museum to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Thank you for spending this time with us, and enjoy your visit.
